sections.title: The Duties of the Kohathites
observations: This section outlines the responsibilities of the Kohathites, one of the Levitical families, in transporting the sacred items of the tabernacle. Their role was crucial as they were entrusted with the most holy objects, including the Ark of the Covenant, the table of showbread, and the lampstand.

The emphasis on the Kohathites' duties highlights the importance of reverence and care in handling sacred things. It serves as a reminder that God desires His people to approach Him with holiness and respect.

sections.title: The Responsibilities of the Gershonites and Merarites
observations: This section describes the roles of the Gershonites and Merarites, who were responsible for transporting the curtains, coverings, and structural components of the tabernacle. Their duties, while different from the Kohathites, were equally important in maintaining the integrity of the worship space.
The division of labor among the Levites illustrates the principle that every member of the community has a unique role to play in the service of God.

importantVerses.commentary: The Kohathites were instructed to cover the holy items before the priests could handle them. This underscores the seriousness of approaching God and the need for proper preparation and reverence.
The instruction to not let the Kohathites die when they approach the holy things emphasizes God's holiness and the need for careful adherence to His commands.

questions: What does this chapter teach us about the holiness of God and our approach to Him?
How can we apply the principle of each member having a unique role in the church today?
What can we learn from the specific instructions given to the Levites regarding their duties?
